    StartersEggsy's pub crackling and scotch eggsPork crackling and sausage wrapped soft eggs, crumbed and fried, with pickled onionsHow to make it500g pork rind4 eggs1 egg, beaten400g pork sausage mince3 tbsp plain flour, for dusting100g panko breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for frying1 jar pickled onions2 tbsp English mustardsalt, to tasteScore the pork rind, salt it well and roast at 240°C until blistered and crisp. Break into pieces.Boil the eggs for 6 minutes, cool in iced water and peel.Wrap each egg in sausage mince, dust in flour, dip in beaten egg and crumb in panko.Fry in the vegetable oil at 170°C for 7 minutes until golden and cooked through.Serve with the crackling, pickled onions and English mustard.Savile Row tea sandwichesCucumber mint cream cheese and smoked salmon dill butter sandwiches, crusts offHow to make it8 slices of white bread150g cream cheese2 tbsp chopped mint1 Lebanese cucumber, thinly sliced150g smoked salmon1 tbsp chopped dill30g soft butterMix the cream cheese with the mint and spread on half the bread.Top with thin cucumber and a second slice of bread.Mash the dill into the butter, spread on the remaining bread and layer with salmon.Trim the crusts and cut into perfectly straight fingers.Mr Pickle's cheddar dog biscuitsHarry's little dog, Mr PickleHow to make itAs written, serves 4Vintage cheddar and cayenne shortbread cut into little terrier shapes, baked golden and crisp, served with a sharp pickled onion relish.Human food only.Rub 100g cold butter into 150g plain flour, then add 120g grated vintage cheddar, a pinch of cayenne and salt.Bring together with 1 tbsp cold water, wrap and chill 30 minutes.Roll to 5mm and cut into small dog shapes.Bake at 180°C for 12 minutes until golden.Chop 6 pickled onions with a spoon of apple chutney for a relish alongside.Potted shrimp on hot toastManners maketh man.
